source_block.parva: Karna Parva · night of the fifteenth day through dawn of the seventeenth · Karna's consecration as senapati, the sixteenth day, and Shalya as Karna's charioteer (with the Udyoga Parva promise)
source_block.bori: BORI CE Karna Parva, Debroy translation vol. 7: 8.6 Ashvatthama proposes Karna and Duryodhana consecrates him; 8.7 the makara-vyuha at sunrise, sixteenth-day fighting to 8.21; 8.22 Karna weighs himself against Arjuna and asks for Shalya; 8.23 Shalya's anger; 8.24 Tripura (Brahma as Shiva's charioteer); 8.25 Shalya accepts on condition his words be borne; 8.26 Shalya mounts the chariot; 8.27 Karna's proclamation of rewards and Shalya's rebuke; 8.28 the crow and the swan; 8.29 Karna knows Krishna and Arjuna, and his curses. Udyoga Parva 5.8: Yudhishthira asks and Shalya promises to dishearten Karna when he becomes his charioteer.
source_block.gita_press: Gita Press Gorakhpur Mahabharata (Hindi, Karna Parva, vulgate numbering ≈ Ganguli): same sequence — Karna-abhisheka at Ashvatthama's counsel, makara-vyuha, Karna's request for Madraraj Shalya, Shalya's wrath, the Tripura-vadha akhyana, Shalya's condition, Karna's proclamation, the kaka-hamsa drishtanta, Karna's reply; Udyoga Parva — Shalya's promise to Yudhishthira.
source_block.ganguli: K.M. Ganguli, Karna Parva §10–42 (vulgate): installation (§10); makara array (§11); sixteenth-day close (§30); Karna's request (§31); Shalya's wrath (§32); Tripura (§33–35); Shalya's condition (§35); Shalya mounts at morning (§36); proclamation and Shalya's scornful laugh (§38); Karna–Shalya exchanges (§39–40); crow and swan (§41); 'That which Vasudeva and Arjuna are is well-known to me' and the curses (§42). Udyoga Parva §8: Shalya's promise to Yudhishthira.
source_block.divergence: Chapter numbers differ: BORI CE compresses the Karna–Shalya exchange into 8.22–8.30 while the vulgate (Ganguli, Gita Press) spreads it over §31–45. The vulgate's long catalogue of rewards (villages, damsels, elephants) is abridged in CE; we narrate only jewels, cows and a golden chariot, which both carry. The vulgate places the crow parable after an extra round of insults (§39–40); CE puts it at 8.28. The mutual insults of Madra and Anga customs (CE 8.27/8.30; Ganguli §40, §44–45) and Karna's two curses (8.29; §42) are omitted for length and left for Ep 17, where the sunken wheel pays them off. The sixteenth-day fighting (Ashvatthama–Arjuna, Bhima–Kshemadhurti and others) is not depicted.
source_block.chosen: Gita Press + BORI/Debroy overlap: Ashvatthama's counsel and Karna's consecration, the makara-vyuha, Karna's request for Shalya, Shalya's anger, Tripura with Brahma as charioteer, Shalya's condition to speak freely, Karna's proclamation, the crow and swan, Karna's resolve, and Shalya's earlier promise to Yudhishthira. Ganguli for English wording.
